obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Dark supporting neutral for text, icons, and strong contrast. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page canvas, card surfaces on light theme, text on dark surfaces

slate.$description: Slate — Muted secondary text, subdued metadata, low-emphasis body copy

hairline.$description: Hairline — Hairline borders, table dividers, input outlines

midnight-ink.$description: Midnight Ink — Dark surface (research section background) — near-black navy that reads as deeper than pure black, giving the dark band a tinted, on-brand cast

periwinkle.$description: Periwinkle — Accent dashes, active indicators, small UI punctuation — the system's only mid-saturation chromatic accent, used sparingly as underlines and section markers

mint-cyan.$description: Mint Cyan — Gray supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis.

sky.$description: Sky — Gray supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis.

blush.$description: Blush — Light supporting surface for subtle backgrounds and section separation.

peach.$description: Peach — Card background — used for the third stat tile, warm counterweight to the cool pinks and blues

the-future.$description: Primary sans-serif for body, nav, headings, and hero — the sole display and text family. Aggressive negative tracking at display sizes (-0.03em at 64px) tightens headlines into compact, near-condensed blocks. Tight line-heights (1.10 at display) keep multi-line headlines visually dense rather than airy.

pp-neue-montreal-mono.$description: Monospace for labels, category badges, button text, and technical metadata — the lab-notebook voice that signals research credibility. Slightly positive tracking (0.005–0.007em) keeps mono caps readable at small sizes.
